summary: In an interview with Fox News Digital, country singer Craig Morgan explains how he balances his music career with re-enlisting in the U.S. Army Reserve at 59, saying he never stopped thinking of himself as a soldier. He discusses the pride, humility and family sacrifice of service, and urges people to serve amid poor recruiting. He also previews his six-song EP "Enlisted," out Oct. 20, with guests including Blake Shelton and Lainey Wilson.
one_line: Country star Craig Morgan discusses re-enlisting in the Army Reserve at 59, balancing it with music, and his collaborative EP "Enlisted."
key_facts: Craig Morgan says he has "never quit being a soldier" and believes "once a soldier, always a soldier."
Morgan spent almost 18 years of his life in the military before re-enlisting in the U.S. Army Reserve.
In July, Morgan was sworn in again at age 59 on stage at the Grand Ole Opry in front of a sold-out audience.
Morgan previously served in the Army and Army Reserve with the 101st and 82nd Airborne Divisions as a staff sergeant and fire support specialist.
Morgan holds airborne, air assault and rappel master certifications.
Morgan has worked with the USO and earned the Army's Outstanding Civilian Service Medal and the USO Merit Award.
Morgan says less than 1% of people in the nation serve in the military and that recruiting is worse than it has ever been.
The biggest challenge of active duty for Morgan was time; he was sometimes away from his family for a year at a time.
Morgan says military service requires more personal planning and coordination than music, since no one makes his military schedule for him.
His EP "Enlisted" debuts Oct. 20 and is a six-song project with renditions of some of his biggest hits plus two new songs.
The EP features Trace Adkins, Luke Combs, Gary LeVox, Jelly Roll, Blake Shelton and Lainey Wilson.
Morgan initially didn't want to re-record his 2005 song "Redneck Yacht Club," but his new song "Raise the Bar" with Billy Dean inspired the project.
Morgan says he knew Lainey Wilson would be a superstar because they wrote together on the same label before she was known.
Blake Shelton had to record his vocals in Los Angeles because of his schedule; Morgan jokingly calls him "a complete idiot all the time."
